$comment: What this catalog's own scaffolding is, so the preview server can rewrite a sticker into the
plain Compose a developer would write — the code behind the 'playground' link on a catalog
card. Read by compose-ai-tools' PlaygroundSourceCleaner; see that file for the rule kinds.
This file is the whole maintenance cost of the feature. Twenty-five entries, for ~400
catalogued components: the ratio is the point. A per-component snippet mapping would drift the
moment a sticker was edited and fail silently when it did, which is exactly what this repo's
README rejects for name-keyed mapping files. Scaffolding is added a few times a year.
A helper with no entry is not silently ignored: the cleaner reports it as residue and the
playground says so in the seed note, so the gap surfaces on the card rather than in a review.

Sticker.$comment: The sticker frame IS a MaterialTheme over the baseline scheme, so renaming is the honest reading. Unwrapping it would leave the snippet unthemed — noisier is better than wrong.

counted.$comment: The click tally exists so no sticker ships a dead handler. To a reader it means: the label you passed, and a click handler.

catalogChoice.$comment: Returns its default on the baked lane by construction, so the default IS what the render on screen was made with.

catalogEnabled.$comment: DROP rather than SUBSTITUTE to true: `enabled = true` is the parameter's own default, and a usage snippet that spells out defaults teaches the reader nothing.

toggleable.$comment: Owned boolean state, read and written through `by`. The helper returns a MutableState precisely so the plain reading is a one-expression swap rather than a declaration rewrite — see CatalogInteractive.kt.

editable.$comment: Owned text state, for text fields.

selectable.$comment: Owned index state, for single-select families (segmented buttons, tabs, navigation bars).

draggable.$comment: Owned float state, for continuous controls (sliders).

multiSelectable.$comment: Owned multi-select state, for families where any number of cells may be on at once. The set update lives at the call site, which is also what a developer would write.

ButtonFrame.$comment: A per-section private frame that exists to keep the RENDER consistent across matrix cells, not to say anything about the component. Its shadowGutter flag is the same kind of thing: room for the elevated button's shadow inside bounds that are otherwise the component's own.
